entries.proposition: Design: four doses (0.5, 2, 7.5, 10 mg/kg/day, fumarate-salt weight) by oral gavage P3 to P10 under 10 percent oxygen; a single hypoxia-plus-vehicle arm and a normoxia arm.
entries.snippet: Doses of clemastine (weighed and dosed based on the clemastine fumarate salt) were: 0.5, 2, 7.5, or 10 mg per kg of body weight.
entries.anchor: Methods / Chronic hypoxia and clemastine treatment

entries.proposition: The minimum effective dose is defined by a conjunction rule: lowest dose that raised myelination above vehicle by all measures tested.
entries.snippet: which we defined as the lowest dose that promoted myelination at P14 above vehicle control levels by all measures tested

entries.proposition: Striatal MBP was significantly above vehicle already at 2 mg/kg (P = 0.003), so the 7.5 mg/kg label rests on the other measures (cell counts, corpus callosum area).
entries.snippet: MBP intensity was significantly higher in the 2 (p = 0.003), 7.5 (p < 0.001) and 10 (p < 0.001) mg/kg hypoxia groups and the normoxia group (p < 0.001)
entries.anchor: Results / Identification of minimum effective dose

entries.proposition: The authors concede only four doses were tested and the true minimum could lie between 2 and 7.5 mg/kg/day.
entries.snippet: It is possible that the true MED lies between 2 and 7.5 mg/kg/day, a dose range that would encompass the exposure provided in the ReBUILD trial.

entries.proposition: Corpus callosum area rose only at 7.5 and 10 mg/kg (P below 0.05).
entries.snippet: Corpus callosum area was significantly increased in hypoxia plus 7.5 and 10 mg/kg clemastine groups and the normoxia group as compared to the vehicle group
entries.anchor: Results / Identification of minimum effective dose

entries.proposition: Total oligodendrocyte-lineage density did not change; the effect is on maturation (mature cell density and OPC fraction).
entries.snippet: Simple main effects analyses showed that treatment group had a statistically significant effect on CC1+ cell density (p < 0.001) and OPCs/SOX10+ cells (p < 0.001), but not SOX10+ cell density (p = 0.08).

entries.proposition: At the minimum dose the g-ratio is a partial rescue only; normoxia remained lower than clemastine-treated.
entries.snippet: We concluded that clemastine treatment at the MED leads to a partial rescue of hypoxia-induced changes in myelin thickness at P14.

entries.proposition: Durability: effect at 10 weeks is described as partial rescue; optic-nerve MBP was not significantly different from vehicle at 10 weeks (only normoxia exceeded vehicle).
entries.snippet: MBP intensity in optic nerves was also higher in normoxia compared to vehicle mice (p < 0.05, one-way ANOVA followed by post hoc Tukey’s test), and was not significantly different between normoxia and clemastine-MED mice.

entries.proposition: Safety statements are observational only: no formal toxicity study, no maximum tolerated dose, no behavioural outcome in this paper; side effects of muscarinic antagonism such as sedation are named by the authors as a limit on neonatal dosing.
entries.snippet: Clemastine has side effects attributed to muscarinic antagonism, such as sedation, that may limit high doses in neonates.

entries.proposition: The authors say the treated mice did not appear sedated and had no overt behavioural abnormality, from visual observation only.
entries.snippet: Treated mice did not appear sedated and did not otherwise have any overt behavioral abnormalities.

entries.proposition: PK at 7.5 mg/kg: Cmax 44 ng/mL at 0.5 h, half-life 4.6 h, trough 0.97 ng/mL; the authors suggest dosing at least every 12 h might optimise effect (a mouse finding).
entries.snippet: The short half-life resulted in low concentrations (0.7 to 1.4 ng/ml) at the end of the 24-h dosing interval and suggests that a shorter dosing interval (such as ≤ every 12 h) could further optimize the pro-myelinating effects of clemastine in rodent models of myelin disorders.

entries.proposition: The PK arm used a separate group of 50 mice (4-5 per time point) under normoxia conditions per the Methods; no PK was measured in hypoxic pups where clearance may differ.
entries.snippet: Male and female C57BL/J mice were dosed by oral gavage with 7.5 mg/kg/day clemastine daily from P3 to P10.

entries.proposition: The Discussion states the minimum-effective-dose exposure is about three times that of the adult MS trial (an adult-human comparison, not a neonatal one).
entries.snippet: provides a daily exposure that is approximately three times higher than the previously demonstrated myelination-promoting dose of clemastine in adult humans with multiple sclerosis
